keep: The idea is named up front: one current through every cell, so the cell that holds least empties first, fills first from flat, and is the one pushed too far.

One picture carries the lesson: six tanks in series, five of 100 Ah and one of an example 80 Ah, one current arrow, Discharge, Charge and Float modes, and a second card of two parallel strings with cable sliders.

Worked numbers from the rule: 40 Ah from every cell after 4 h at 10 A; the string gives 80 Ah with 100 Ah stranded; 7 h for a 70 Ah cell; 13.38 V held on float with the band 2.18 to 2.33 V; 2.38 V leaves 2.20 V for each of the others; 57 A and 43 A on 2 and 6 mOhm cables; 23.8 V at 100 A for two blocks in series; 2400 Wh either way.

Each named slip has a DO screen with a hint per wrong pick: sharing by size (1), the average cell (3), the empty cell resting (5), the full cell stopping the current (7), a good total meaning good cells (9), equal parallel shares (11), resistances not adding (12), series as more energy (13), a charge curing the cell (14).
The charge case is honest: the weak cell fills first when the string starts flat, said in the takeaway, and the ignores panel says how the reversed cell and recharge efficiency are simplified.
New sources (EnerSys band and parallel rule, BU-502 reversal short, BU-403 float starving, BU-803a resurfacing) were checked by tools/eval/sources.mjs and appended to research.json.
fix: Causal step skipped: why the weak cell's float voltage climbs. Say its plates take no more charge, so its voltage climbs towards the gassing voltage met in lesson 5.
False absolute: 'Only the cell readings can' find a bad cell. Specific gravity and lesson 7's trends find them too. Say cell-by-cell readings can.
False absolute: 'That overcharge corrodes its positive grid'. Grid corrosion follows prolonged overcharge. Say kept up, it corrodes the positive grid.
The brief names the effect but not its cause. Put the one current draining all six tanks equally into it.
Explain's charge paragraph does not say why a string might start flat. Say a deep discharge can leave every cell flat.

shape.ruleInWords: yes: one current through every cell, so each gives and takes the same ampere-hours; the string gives its smallest cell's ampere-hours; on float the charger holds the total; parallel strings share inversely to path resistance
shape.workedExampleWithRealNumbers: yes (80 Ah from five 100 Ah and one 80 Ah at 10 A; 13.38 V and 2.20 V per cell; 57 A and 43 A; 12 cells at 26.76 V with one at 2.08 V)
shape.misconceptionShownFailing: yes: the good total (9), the average cell (3), the equal parallel share (11), series as more energy (13), the charge that cures (14)
shape.analogyWithBreaks: yes: a radial run partly in smaller cable, where one current sets the smallest length as the limit; breaks because a cable limits current, not ampere-hours, and never reverses
shape.practice: yes: steps, rule of thumb, worked example, common mistakes
